questions.question: Which property distinguishes a homogeneous mixture from a heterogeneous mixture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uniform composition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **mixture** consists of two or more different substances that are physically combined but not chemically bonded. The primary way to classify these is based on how the substances are distributed within the sample.
 
• A **homogeneous mixture** is characterized by a **uniform composition** throughout its mass. This means that any sample taken from the mixture will have the exact same proportions of its components. Examples include **saltwater** or **clean air**.
 
• A **heterogeneous mixture** possesses a **non-uniform composition**, meaning its components are not evenly distributed. Different regions of the mixture may have different properties and compositions. Examples include a **salad** or **oil and water**.
 
• The term **"phase"** is often used to distinguish them: a homogeneous mixture consists of a **single phase** (solid, liquid, or gas), while a heterogeneous mixture consists of **two or more phases** that remain physically separate.
 
• Regarding the other options: **Chemical reactions** are not a property of mixtures, as mixtures are formed through **physical changes**. A **fixed boiling point** is a characteristic of **pure substances** (elements or compounds), not mixtures. **High density** is a physical property of specific materials but does not determine whether a mixture is homogeneous or heterogeneous.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Homogeneous Mixtures (Solutions):**
 
 
• These are often referred to as **solutions**. A solution consists of a **solute** (the substance being dissolved) and a **solvent** (the medium in which it is dissolved).
 
• In a liquid solution like **sugar-water**, the sugar particles are so small (typically less than **1 nanometer**) that they cannot be seen even with a microscope and do not settle over time.
 
• **Alloys**, such as **brass** (copper and zinc) or **steel** (iron and carbon), are considered solid homogeneous mixtures.
 
 
 
• **Heterogeneous Mixtures (Suspensions and Colloids):**
 
 
• **Suspensions** are heterogeneous mixtures where the particles are large enough to be seen and will eventually **settle out** due to gravity (e.g., **sand in water**).
 
• **Colloids** occupy a middle ground; they may appear homogeneous to the naked eye but are heterogeneous at a microscopic level (e.g., **milk** or **fog**). They exhibit the **Tyndall Effect**, which is the scattering of light by particles.
 
 
 
• **Separation Techniques:**
 
 
• Because mixtures are physical combinations, they can be separated by **physical methods**.
 
• **Homogeneous mixtures** usually require methods that involve phase changes, such as **distillation** or **evaporation**, to separate the components.
 
• **Heterogeneous mixtures** can often be separated by simpler mechanical means such as **filtration**, **decantation**, or using a **centrifuge**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Pure Substances:**
 
 
• A **pure substance** has constant physical and chemical properties. For instance, **distilled water** always boils at **100 degrees Celsius** at sea level.
 
• In contrast, mixtures do not have a **fixed boiling or melting point**; they generally boil or melt over a **range of temperatures** depending on the concentration of the components.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is always formed during a neutralization reaction between a strong acid and a strong base?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Salt and water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **neutralization reaction** is a specific type of chemical reaction where an **acid** and a **base** react with each other to produce a **salt** and **water**.
 
• When a **strong acid** (like **Hydrochloric acid**) reacts with a **strong base** (like **Sodium hydroxide**), the **hydrogen ions (H+)** from the acid and the **hydroxide ions (OH-)** from the base combine to form **neutral water (H2O)** molecules.
 
• The **anion** (negative ion) from the acid and the **cation** (positive ion) from the base combine to form an **ionic compound** called a **salt** (e.g., **Sodium chloride**). ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• Neutralization reactions between **strong acids** and **strong bases** typically result in a solution with a **pH of 7** at **25 degrees Celsius**, indicating a **neutral solution**.
 
• These reactions are inherently **exothermic**, meaning they release **thermal energy** or heat during the process.
 
• The formation of **hydrogen gas** typically occurs during the reaction of an **acid with a metal**, not during a standard acid-base neutralization. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• While **water** is always formed, it is never the **only** product; the **counter-ions** must form a salt. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The production of **carbon dioxide** alongside salt and water occurs only when the base is a **carbonate** or **bicarbonate**, rather than a simple strong base like a **metal hydroxide**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Strong Acids:**
 
 
• These are substances that **completely ionize** in an aqueous solution, meaning they release all their available **hydrogen ions**.
 
• Examples include **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)**, **Sulfuric acid (H2SO4)**, and **Nitric acid (HNO3)**.
 
• They have a very **low pH** value, usually between **0 and 3**.
 
 
 
• **Strong Bases:**
 
 
• These are substances that **completely dissociate** in water to release **hydroxide ions (OH-)**.
 
• Common examples include **Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)**, also known as **caustic soda**, and **Potassium hydroxide (KOH)**.
 
• They have a **high pH** value, typically ranging from **12 to 14**.
 
 
 
• **The pH Scale:**
 
 
• The **pH scale** is a logarithmic scale used to measure the **acidity** or **alkalinity** of a solution.
 
• It ranges from **0 to 14**, where **7** is neutral, values **below 7** are acidic, and values **above 7** are basic.
 
 
 
• **Titration:**
 
 
• This is a common laboratory method where a **neutralization reaction** is used to determine the unknown **concentration** of an acid or a base.
 
• An **indicator** (like **phenolphthalein**) is often used to signal the **equivalence point**, where the moles of acid equal the moles of base.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Heat of Neutralization:** For any **strong acid** and **strong base** reaction, the **enthalpy change** is approximately constant at **-57.3 kJ/mol** because the essential reaction is always the formation of water from **H+** and **OH-** ions.
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• **Antacids:** Used to treat **acidity** in the stomach by neutralizing excess **HCl** with a weak base like **Magnesium hydroxide**.
 
• **Soil Treatment:** If the soil is too **acidic**, farmers add **quicklime (calcium oxide)** or **slaked lime (calcium hydroxide)** to neutralize it for better crop growth.
 
• **Wastewater Treatment:** Industrial effluents containing acids are neutralized with **lime** before being discharged into water bodies to prevent **environmental damage**.
 
 
 
• **Ionic Equation:** The net ionic equation for a strong acid-strong base neutralization is always: **H+ (aq) + OH- (aq) → H2O (l)**.
</ul

questions.question: Animals with high energy needs and constant body temperature, like birds and mammals, have __________ chambered hearts.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Four**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Birds** and **mammals** are **warm-blooded** (homeothermic) animals, meaning they maintain a **constant body temperature** regardless of the external environment.
 
• To maintain this internal temperature and support high levels of activity, these animals have **high energy needs**, which require a very efficient supply of **oxygen** to the body cells.
 
• A **four-chambered heart** consists of **two atria** and **two ventricles**, which ensures the complete physical separation of **oxygenated blood** (rich in oxygen) and **deoxygenated blood** (rich in carbon dioxide).
 
• This separation prevents the mixing of blood, allowing for a highly efficient **double circulation** system where **oxygen** is delivered to the tissues at a high pressure and rate. ***Hence, the statement regarding four-chambered hearts is correct.***
 
• The **left side** of the heart handles oxygenated blood coming from the **lungs**, while the **right side** manages deoxygenated blood returning from the **body tissues**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Two-Chambered Heart:**
 
 
• This type of heart is typically found in **fishes**.
 
• It consists of **one atrium** and **one ventricle**.
 
• The blood is pumped to the **gills**, where it is oxygenated, and then flows directly to the rest of the body. This is known as **single circulation**.
 
 
 
• **Three-Chambered Heart:**
 
 
• Found in **amphibians** (like frogs) and most **reptiles** (like lizards and snakes).
 
• It consists of **two atria** and **one single ventricle**.
 
• In the single ventricle, there is some **mixing** of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, which is less efficient but sufficient for these **cold-blooded** (poikilothermic) animals with lower metabolic rates.
 
 
 
• **Exceptional Cases in Reptiles:**
 
 
• While most reptiles have three chambers, **crocodiles** and **alligators** are notable exceptions as they possess a **four-chambered heart**, similar to birds and mammals.
 
 
 
• **Double Circulation:**
 
 
• This refers to the blood passing through the heart **twice** during one complete cycle of the body.
 
• It includes **pulmonary circulation** (between heart and lungs) and **systemic circulation** (between heart and the rest of the body).
 
• This mechanism is vital for maintaining the **high metabolic rate** and **homeostasis** in mammals and birds.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Energy and Temperature:** Animals that do not use energy to maintain their body temperature (cold-blooded) can tolerate some mixing of blood, but for **homeotherms**, the **four chambers** are an evolutionary necessity.
 
• **Ventricle Evolution:** The evolution from a **single ventricle** (in fish) to a **partially divided ventricle** (in reptiles) and finally to a **completely divided ventricle** (in mammals and birds) reflects the increasing demand for **metabolic efficiency**.
 
• **Left Ventricle:** In a four-chambered heart, the **left ventricle** usually has the **thickest muscular wall** because it must pump blood to the entire body.
</ul

questions.question: Which part of the food-conducting complex tissue in plants is tubular and has perforated walls?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sieve tube**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Phloem** is a **complex permanent tissue** in vascular plants that functions as the **food-conducting complex tissue**, transporting **organic nutrients** (mainly **sucrose**) from the leaves to other parts of the plant.
 
• **Sieve tubes** are the primary conducting elements of the phloem. They are **long, tubular structures** arranged longitudinally and are characterized by having **perforated walls**.
 
• The end walls of sieve tube cells are called **sieve plates**, which are perforated in a sieve-like manner to allow the continuous flow of food materials between adjacent cells. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• A mature **sieve tube** element possesses a **peripheral layer of cytoplasm** and a **large vacuole** but **lacks a nucleus**. This structural adaptation allows for more efficient transport of nutrients.
 
• The functions of sieve tubes are controlled by the **nucleus of companion cells**, which are specialized parenchyma cells closely associated with them through **pit fields**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Components of Phloem:**
 
 
• **Companion Cells:** These are specialized **parenchymatous cells** that help maintain the **pressure gradient** in the sieve tubes. They are living cells with a **dense cytoplasm** and a **distinct nucleus**.
 
• **Phloem Parenchyma:** This consists of **elongated, tapering cylindrical cells** that have dense cytoplasm and a nucleus. Their primary function is the **storage of food** and other substances like **resins, latex, and mucilage**.
 
• **Phloem Fibers:** Also known as **bast fibers**, these are made of **sclerenchymatous cells**. They are generally absent in primary phloem but present in secondary phloem. They provide **mechanical strength** and are **dead at maturity**.
 
 
 
• **Vascular Bundle Context:**
 
 
• In addition to **phloem**, plants possess **xylem**, which is responsible for the conduction of **water and minerals** from roots to leaves.
 
• Unlike phloem, which conducts material **bidirectionally**, xylem typically facilitates **unidirectional transport**.
 
• **Sieve cells** are found in **gymnosperms**, whereas **sieve tubes** are characteristic of **angiosperms**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **sieve plate** is the specific perforated end wall, but the **sieve tube** is the overall "part" or unit of the tissue that is described as **tubular** and having these **perforated walls**.
 
• **Phloem transport** is an active process that requires energy in the form of **ATP** to load sucrose into the sieve tube elements.
 
• The **first formed primary phloem** consists of narrow sieve tubes and is referred to as **protophloem**, whereas the later formed phloem has bigger sieve tubes and is called **metaphloem**.
 
• The **sieve tube elements** are unique because they are **living cells** that function without a nucleus, a condition known as being **enucleated** at maturity.
</ul

questions.question: What is the advantage of combining DNA from two different individuals in sexually reproducing animals?

options.text: It reduces the need for specialized reproductive organs.
It eliminates errors in DNA copying.
It increases genetic variation within the population.
It speeds up the reproduction process.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It increases genetic variation within the population**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sexual reproduction** involves the fusion of specialized cells called **gametes** (sperm and egg) from two different individuals, which combines their **DNA** to create a new organism.
 
• The most significant advantage of this process is the generation of **genetic variation**. Because the offspring receives a unique mix of **alleles** from both parents, they are genetically distinct from their parents and siblings.
 
• This **variation** is essential for the process of **evolution**. It provides the raw material upon which **natural selection** acts, allowing populations to adapt to changing environments, diseases, or predators. ***Hence, the statement "It increases genetic variation within the population" is correct.***
 
• Combining **DNA** from two individuals allows for **genetic recombination**. During **meiosis**, homologous chromosomes exchange segments, further increasing the diversity of the genetic code passed to the next generation.
 
• While **asexual reproduction** is more efficient in stable environments, it produces clones. A lack of **genetic diversity** in asexual populations makes them highly susceptible to being wiped out by a single environmental change or pathogen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reproductive Complexity**: Contrary to reducing the need for specialized parts, **sexual reproduction** actually requires **specialized reproductive organs** (such as ovaries and testes) and complex hormonal systems to facilitate the production and fusion of gametes. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **DNA Copying Errors**: **DNA replication** is a biological process that naturally involves a small rate of error, leading to **mutations**. Sexual reproduction does not eliminate these errors; in fact, mutations are the ultimate source of all **genetic variation**, though sexual reproduction helps reshuffle these mutations. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Reproductive Speed**: **Sexual reproduction** is generally much **slower** than asexual reproduction. It requires finding a mate, the energetic cost of producing gametes, and often a lengthy **gestation** or incubation period. **Asexual reproduction** (like binary fission in bacteria) is far more rapid. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• **The Red Queen Hypothesis**: This evolutionary theory suggests that **sexual reproduction** is maintained because it allows hosts to evolve new **genetic defenses** rapidly enough to keep pace with the evolution of parasites and pathogens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Meiosis**: This is the key cellular process behind sexual reproduction. It involves two rounds of division to produce **haploid** cells (containing half the **chromosomes** of the parent).
 
• **Independent Assortment**: During **meiosis**, the random distribution of maternal and paternal chromosomes into gametes ensures that every gamete is unique, contributing to the **genotypic diversity** of the offspring.
 
• **Adaptability**: In a population with high **genetic variation**, there is a higher probability that some individuals will possess traits (such as **drought resistance** or **immunity** to a specific virus) that allow them to survive a catastrophe that might kill others.
 
• **Muller's Ratchet**: This concept explains that asexual populations tend to accumulate **deleterious mutations** over time because they cannot "purge" them through recombination. **Sexual reproduction** helps solve this problem by producing some offspring with fewer harmful mutations than their parents.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements about a proton is correct ?

options.text: A proton is neutral in charge and has mass equal to an electron
A proton is positively charged and its mass is taken as one unit
A proton is negatively charged and has very small mass
A proton is positively charged and mass is 1/2000 of a hydrogen atom

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A proton is positively charged and its mass is taken as one unit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **proton** is a subatomic particle that carries a **positive electrical charge** of **+1e** (approximately **1.602 x 10⁻¹⁹ Coulombs**). ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The **mass of a proton** is approximately **1.672 x 10⁻²⁷ kg**. In the context of atomic chemistry, this mass is considered to be **1 unit** (roughly **1 atomic mass unit or amu**).
 
• **Statement 1** suggests that a proton is neutral and has mass equal to an electron. This is incorrect because **neutrons** are the particles that are **neutral**, and a proton is about **1836 times heavier** than an electron. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 3** claims that a proton is negatively charged. This is the characteristic of an **electron**, not a proton. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 4** mentions that a proton's mass is **1/2000** of a **hydrogen atom**. In reality, a hydrogen atom (specifically the **protium** isotope) consists of exactly **one proton** and **one electron**. Since the electron's mass is negligible, the proton's mass is nearly **equal** to that of a hydrogen atom, not a fraction of it. It is the **electron** whose mass is approximately **1/1840** (often rounded to **1/2000**) of a proton. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Discovery of Protons:** 
 
 
• In **1886**, **E. Goldstein** discovered the presence of new radiations in a gas discharge which he called **canal rays**. These rays were positively charged radiations.
 
• Later, **Ernest Rutherford** is credited with the discovery of the **nucleus** and identifying the proton as a fundamental particle in the year **1917** to **1919** through his gold foil experiment and subsequent nitrogen-alpha particle experiments.
 
 
 
• **Location in the Atom:**
 
 
• Protons are located inside the **nucleus** at the center of the atom. 
 
• Along with **neutrons**, they are collectively referred to as **nucleons**.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Number (Z):**
 
 
• The **Atomic Number** of an element is defined by the total **number of protons** present in the nucleus of its atom.
 
• For example, **Carbon** has an atomic number of **6** because it contains **6 protons**.
 
 
 
• **Stability:**
 
 
• The proton is a **stable particle**, meaning it does not decay into other particles under normal conditions. Its estimated **half-life** is greater than **10³⁴ years**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison of Subatomic Particles:**
 
 
• **Proton:** Positive charge (**+1**), Mass ~ **1 amu**, Location: **Inside Nucleus**.
 
• **Neutron:** Neutral charge (**0**), Mass ~ **1 amu**, Location: **Inside Nucleus**.
 
• **Electron:** Negative charge (**-1**), Mass ~ **1/1840 amu** (negligible), Location: **Outside Nucleus** in orbits.
 
 
 
• **Charge Neutrality:** In a **neutral atom**, the number of **protons** is exactly **equal** to the number of **electrons**, making the net charge of the atom **zero**.
</ul

questions.question: For a resistor with constant resistance, the magnitude of heat produced is directly proportional to which of the following?

options.text: Square of the current flowing through the resistor

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Square of the current flowing through the resistor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The physical phenomenon where heat is generated by an electric current passing through a conductor is known as the **Heating Effect of Electric Current**.
 
• According to **Joule’s Law of Heating**, the heat produced in a **resistor** is directly proportional to the **square of the current** (**I²**) for a given **resistance**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The law also states that the heat produced is directly proportional to the **resistance** (**R**) for a given current. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect*** in this context because the question specifies a **constant resistance**, making length a factor already accounted for in the constant value.
 
• Furthermore, the magnitude of heat is directly proportional to the **time** (**t**) for which the **electric current** flows through the **resistor**.
 
• The mathematical representation of this law is **H = I²Rt**, where **H** represents **Heat** in **Joules**, **I** represents **Current** in **Amperes**, **R** represents **Resistance** in **Ohms**, and **t** represents **Time** in **Seconds**.
 
• Heat is not linearly proportional to the **current**, but rather to its square; thus, if the **current** is doubled, the **heat produced** increases by **4 times**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **James Prescott Joule**: This law was first deduced by the **English physicist** **James Prescott Joule** in the year **1841**. His work led to the **First Law of Thermodynamics**.
 
• **Electric Power**: The rate at which **electrical energy** is dissipated as **heat** is called **Electric Power** (**P**). It is expressed as **P = I²R** or **P = VI**, where **V** is the **potential difference**.
 
• **Applications**: The heating effect is utilized in various household appliances such as **electric heaters**, **electric irons**, **geysers**, **toasters**, and **electric kettles**.
 
• **Filament Lamps**: In an **incandescent light bulb**, the **Tungsten filament** (having a high **melting point** of **3380 degrees Celsius**) is heated to such a high temperature that it starts glowing and emitting light.
 
• **Electric Fuse**: A **safety device** used in **electrical circuits** that works on the **heating effect of current**. It is made of an alloy (like **tin-lead**) with a **low melting point** to protect the circuit from **short circuits** or **overloading**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Resistance (R)**: It is the opposition offered by a **material** to the flow of **electric current**. The **SI unit** is **Ohm** (represented by **Ω**). While **resistance** depends on **length** and **area**, the question assumes it to be **constant**.
 
• **Density of Material**: The **density** of the **resistor** material does not directly appear in the **Joule’s Law** formula for heat dissipation. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Energy Conversion**: In a purely **resistive circuit**, the entire **electrical energy** consumed is converted into **thermal energy** (heat).
 
• **Nichrome**: A commonly used alloy in **heating elements** because of its high **resistivity** and ability to withstand high temperatures without **oxidation**.
 
• **Numerical Fact**: **1 calorie** is equal to approximately **4.184 Joules**. Sometimes **heat** in these problems is requested in **calories**, requiring a division by **4.184**.

5f:

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about a base in an aqueous solution?

options.text: They react with metals to produce hydrogen gas.
They produce OH⁻ ions in water.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They produce OH⁻ ions in water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Arrhenius theory** of acids and bases, a **base** is a substance that dissociates in **aqueous solution** to form **hydroxide ions (OH⁻)**. This increase in **hydroxyl ion** concentration is the defining characteristic of an Arrhenius base. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Bases** have the property of turning **red litmus paper blue**. The statement that they turn blue litmus red is a characteristic of **acids**, not bases. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The physical property of **sour taste** is associated with **acids** (such as **citric acid** in lemons). **Bases** are known for having a **bitter taste** and a **slippery or soapy feel** to the touch. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• While certain strong bases like **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)** can react with specific active metals like **Zinc (Zn)** or **Aluminum (Al)** to produce **Hydrogen gas (H₂)**, this is not a general property of all bases. Generally, the reaction with metals to produce hydrogen is a classic identifying feature of **acids**. ***Hence, statement 1 is not the primary defining truth for bases in general.***
 
• Common examples of bases in **aqueous solutions** include **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)**, **Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)₂)**, and **Potassium Hydroxide (KOH)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The pH Scale:** The strength of a base is measured on the **pH scale**. Bases have a **pH value** ranging from **above 7 to 14**. A **pH of 7** is considered **neutral** (like pure water), while a **pH of 14** indicates a very **strong alkali**.
 
• **Strong vs. Weak Bases:**
 
 
• **Strong Bases:** These are compounds that **completely ionize** or dissociate into their component ions in **water**. Examples include **Group 1** hydroxides like **Lithium Hydroxide (LiOH)**.
 
• **Weak Bases:** These do not dissociate completely in **aqueous solution**. **Ammonia (NH₃)** is a classic example of a **weak base**.
 
 
 
• **Alkali:** A base that is **soluble in water** is specifically called an **alkali**. It is important to note that while all **alkalis are bases**, not all bases are alkalis, as some do not dissolve in water.
 
• **Neutralization Reaction:** When a **base** reacts with an **acid**, they undergo a **neutralization reaction** to produce **salt and water**. For example, **HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O**.
 
• **Uses of Bases:**
 
 
• **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)** is used in the manufacture of **soap, paper, and synthetic fibers** like rayon.
 
• **Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)₂)**, also known as **slaked lime**, is used in the manufacture of **bleaching powder** and for **whitewashing**.
 
• **Magnesium Hydroxide (Mg(OH)₂)** is commonly used as an **antacid** to neutralize excess stomach acid.

• **Alkaline Potassium Permanganate** (**KMnO4**) and **Acidified Potassium Dichromate** (**K2Cr2O7**) are both classified as **strong oxidizing agents**. They are capable of donating oxygen or removing hydrogen from organic substrates.
 
• When **Ethanol** is treated with these reagents and subjected to **Heat**, it undergoes a two-step oxidation process. It first forms **Ethanal** (an **aldehyde**), which is then rapidly oxidized further because of the strength of the reagents.
 
• The final product of this complete oxidation is **Ethanoic acid** (**CH3COOH**). In this transformation, the **carbon chain length** remains constant; since the starting alcohol has **two carbon atoms**, the resulting carboxylic acid also has **two carbon atoms**. ***Hence, the product is Ethanoic acid.***

__
 
• **Megaphones**, **horns**, and **stethoscopes** are instruments designed to **produce, transmit, and amplify sound** signals using the physical principle of **multiple reflection of sound**.
 
• In these devices, a tube or a conical shape is used to **reflect sound waves** repeatedly in such a way that the waves are guided in a specific direction toward the audience or the listener's ear. ***Hence, the statement regarding their use to produce, transmit, and amplify sound is correct.***
 
• A **megaphone** or **speaking-trumpet** consists of a **conical opening** that prevents the **sound energy** from spreading out in all directions, effectively **amplifying** the sound intensity in the forward direction.
 
• A **stethoscope** is a medical instrument used by doctors to listen to sounds produced within the body, primarily the **heart** and **lungs**. It works by transmitting the sound from the chest piece to the earpieces through **multiple reflections** inside the connecting rubber or plastic tubes.
 
• The primary function of these devices is not to block sound or change its pitch, but to ensure that the **amplitude** and **clarity** of the sound reaching the observer are significantly increased.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Reverberation:** This refers to the **persistence of sound** due to repeated reflections in a large hall or auditorium. Excessive **reverberation** is usually reduced by using **sound-absorbent materials** like compressed fiberboards or rough plaster.
 
• **Pitch vs. Loudness:** **Pitch** depends on the **frequency** of the sound wave, while **loudness** or **amplification** depends on the **amplitude**. The devices mentioned in the question primarily affect the **loudness** and direction rather than the frequency (pitch).

• **Sound Boards:** Sometimes, a **curved soundboard** is placed behind the speaker in a large hall so that the sound, after reflecting from the **soundboard**, spreads evenly across the width of the hall.
 
• **Applications of Multiple Reflection:** Apart from medical and public speaking tools, the principle of **multiple reflection** is also utilized in **ultrasonography** and **SONAR** (Sound Navigation and Ranging) technologies used for underwater communication and detection.

• When the **brakes** are applied suddenly, the car comes to a halt or slows down due to the **frictional force** between the tires and the road, but this force is not directly applied to the **upper body** of the passengers.
 
• Due to the property of **Inertia of Motion**, the passengers' bodies tend to maintain their **original state of motion** (moving forward), while the car (and the lower part of the passenger's body in contact with the seat) slows down.
 
• The **air inside the car** does not have enough mass or pressure change to push passengers forward significantly during braking. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• The tendency to move forward is a direct result of the body's **inertia** resisting the change in **velocity**. *Hence, statement 2 is correct.*
 
• **Gravity** acts vertically downward and does not pull passengers forward horizontally when brakes are applied. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*
 
• **Brakes** apply a **backward force** (deceleration) on the car, not a forward force on the passengers. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*

• **Types of Inertia:**
 
 
• **Inertia of Rest:** The tendency of a body to remain at **rest**. For example, when a stationary bus starts suddenly, passengers fall **backward** because their lower body moves with the bus, but the upper body tries to stay at rest.
 
• **Inertia of Motion:** The tendency of a body to remain in **uniform motion**. The car braking scenario is a classic example of this.
 
• **Inertia of Direction:** The tendency of a body to resist a change in its **direction of motion**. For example, when a car takes a sharp **curve**, passengers are thrown toward the **outside** of the curve.
 
 
 
• **Mass and Inertia:**
 
 
• The **inertia** of an object is measured by its **mass**. An object with a larger **mass** (like a truck) has more inertia and is harder to stop or start than an object with a smaller **mass** (like a bicycle).
 
• The **SI unit** of mass is the **kilogram (kg)**.
 
 
 
• **Applications in Safety:**
 
 
• **Seatbelts** are designed to provide the necessary **external force** to stop the passenger's body from moving forward due to inertia, preventing them from hitting the **windshield** or dashboard.
 
• **Airbags** provide a cushion to increase the **time of impact**, thereby reducing the **force** exerted on the passenger during a sudden stop.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Newton** published these laws in his famous book **"Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica"** in the year **1687**.

questions.question: For a body moving with uniform velocity, the acceleration is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**zero**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acceleration** is defined as the rate of change of **velocity** with respect to **time**. In physics, it is a **vector quantity** that describes how quickly an object's velocity is changing.
 
• A body is said to be moving with **uniform velocity** when it covers equal **displacements** in equal intervals of **time**, meaning both its **magnitude (speed)** and **direction** remain **constant** over time.
 
• The mathematical formula for **acceleration (a)** is given by **a = (v - u) / t**, where **v** represents the **final velocity**, **u** represents the **initial velocity**, and **t** is the **time interval**.
 
• In the case of **uniform velocity**, the **initial velocity** is exactly equal to the **final velocity** (**u = v**). Therefore, the change in velocity (**v - u**) is **0**.
 
• Because the change in velocity is **0**, the result of the acceleration formula becomes **0 / t**, which equals **zero**. ***Hence, for a body moving with uniform velocity, the acceleration is always zero.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Velocity vs. Speed**: While **speed** is a **scalar quantity** (only magnitude), **velocity** is a **vector quantity**. A change in either the **speed** or the **direction** of motion will result in a change in **velocity**, thereby producing **acceleration**.
 
• **Uniform Circular Motion**: This is a unique case where an object moves at a **constant speed** but its **velocity** is constantly changing because its **direction** is changing at every point. In this scenario, the acceleration is **not zero**; it is called **centripetal acceleration**.
 
• **Graphical Representation**: 
 
 
• In a **Velocity-Time (v-t) graph**, **uniform velocity** is represented by a **horizontal straight line** parallel to the **time axis**. The **slope** of a **v-t graph** represents **acceleration**; since the slope of a horizontal line is **0**, the acceleration is **zero**.
 
• In a **Position-Time (s-t) graph**, **uniform velocity** is represented by a **straight line** with a **constant slope**. The **slope** of this graph represents the **velocity** of the object.
 
 
 
• **Types of Acceleration**: 
 
 
• **Positive Acceleration**: Occurs when the **velocity** of an object **increases** over **time**.
 
• **Negative Acceleration (Retardation/Deceleration)**: Occurs when the **velocity** of an object **decreases** over **time**.
 
• **Zero Acceleration**: Occurs when the object is at **rest** or moving with **uniform velocity**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion**: Also known as the **Law of Inertia**, it states that an object will remain in its state of **rest** or **uniform motion** in a **straight line** unless compelled to change 그 state by an **external force**. This implies that if **acceleration** is **zero**, the **net external force** acting on the body is also **zero**.
 
• **Newton's Second Law**: Defined by the equation **F = ma** (Force = mass x acceleration). This relationship confirms that if **acceleration (a)** is **0**, the **resultant force (F)** must be **0**, regardless of the object's **mass**.
 
• **Units and Dimensions**: The **S.I. unit** of **acceleration** is **m/s² (meters per second squared)**. Its **dimensional formula** is **[M⁰ L¹ T⁻²]**.
 
• **Instantaneous Acceleration**: This refers to the **acceleration** of an object at a specific **instant of time**, calculated by taking the **derivative of velocity** with respect to **time (dv/dt)**. For **uniform velocity**, this derivative is always **0**.

questions.question: Which of the following molecules is split apart by higher energy ultraviolet for formation of ozone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oxygen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ozone (O3)** is a molecule composed of **three oxygen atoms**. It is formed naturally in the upper atmosphere through a photochemical process.
 
• The formation of **Ozone** begins when **higher-energy ultraviolet (UV) radiation**, specifically **UV-C** rays from the sun, strike an **Oxygen molecule (O2)**.
 
• This high-energy radiation has enough energy to break the chemical bond holding the **Oxygen molecule** together, splitting it into two individual **Oxygen atoms (O + O)**. This process is known as **photolysis** or **photodissociation**.
 
• These freed, highly reactive **Oxygen atoms** then quickly collide and combine with another intact **Oxygen molecule (O2)** to form **Ozone (O3)**.
 
• The presence of a third body (usually **Nitrogen** or another **Oxygen molecule**) is often required in the collision to absorb excess energy and stabilize the newly formed **Ozone** molecule.
 
• Other options like **Zinc**, **Iron**, and **Sodium** are **metallic elements** that do not exist as gaseous diatomic molecules in the Earth's atmosphere to participate in this specific UV-driven ozone formation cycle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Chapman Cycle:** This is the set of four reactions, first proposed by **Sydney Chapman** in **1930**, that describes how **Ozone** is continuously regenerated in the Earth's **stratosphere**.
 
• **Location of Ozone:** About **90%** of the Earth's ozone is found in the **Stratosphere** (the atmospheric layer between **10 km and 50 km** above the Earth's surface). This region is commonly called the **Ozone Layer**.
 
• **Functions of the Ozone Layer:** It acts as a protective shield by absorbing **97% to 99%** of the sun's medium-frequency **ultraviolet light** (from about **200 nm to 315 nm** wavelength), which otherwise would potentially damage exposed life forms on **Earth**.
 
• **Types of UV Radiation:** 
 
 
• **UV-A (315–400 nm):** Not absorbed by **Ozone**; reaches the surface.
 
• **UV-B (280–315 nm):** Partially absorbed by **Ozone**; causes sunburn and skin cancer.
 
• **UV-C (100–280 nm):** Completely absorbed by **Oxygen** and **Ozone** in the upper atmosphere; it is the most energetic and dangerous type.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Measurement:** The concentration of **Ozone** in the atmosphere is measured in **Dobson Units (DU)**. A typical baseline value is approximately **300 DU**.
 
• **Ozone Hole:** This refers to the thinning of the **Ozone layer**, primarily over **Antarctica**, caused by **Ozone-Depleting Substances (ODS)** like **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)**, **halons**, and **carbon tetrachloride**.
 
• **Montreal Protocol:** An international treaty signed in **1987** (effective from **1989**) designed to protect the **Ozone layer** by phasing out the production of numerous substances that are responsible for ozone depletion.
 
• **World Ozone Day:** Observed every year on **September 16th** to commemorate the date of the signing of the **Montreal Protocol**.
 
• **Ground-level Ozone:** While **stratospheric ozone** is "good" for protection, **tropospheric ozone** (ground-level) is a "bad" pollutant and a key constituent of **smog**, formed by the reaction of **NOx** and **VOCs** in the presence of sunlight.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following rays is NOT used to locate the image formed by a spherical mirror?

options.text: A ray passing through the focus that reflects parallel to the principal axis
A ray passing through the center of curvature that reflects back along the same path
A ray perpendicular to the principal axis that reflects through the focus
A ray parallel to the principal axis that reflects through the focus

questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**A ray perpendicular to the principal axis that reflects through the focus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To locate the image formed by a **spherical mirror**, certain specific rays are used because their paths after **reflection** are predictable based on the **laws of reflection**.
 
• **Ray 1 (Parallel Ray):** A ray that is **parallel to the principal axis** will, after reflection, pass through the **principal focus** in a **concave mirror** or appear to diverge from the focus in a **convex mirror**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• **Ray 2 (Ray through Focus):** A ray passing through the **principal focus** of a concave mirror (or directed towards the focus of a convex mirror) will emerge **parallel to the principal axis** after reflection. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Ray 3 (Ray through Center of Curvature):** A ray passing through the **center of curvature** (C) of a spherical mirror reflects back along the **same path**. This happens because the ray strikes the mirror surface **normally** (at an **angle of incidence** of **0 degrees**). ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Incorrect Ray:** A ray **perpendicular to the principal axis** is a vertical ray that does not follow the standard geometric path to reflect through the focus. For a ray to reflect through the focus, it must be **parallel** to the principal axis, not perpendicular. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect and is the ray NOT used.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is A ray perpendicular to the principal axis that reflects through the focus.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Components of Spherical Mirrors:**
 
 
• **Pole (P):** The center of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror is called the **pole**. It lies on the surface of the mirror.
 
• **Center of Curvature (C):** The reflecting surface forms a part of a sphere. The center of this sphere is the **center of curvature**. For a **concave mirror**, it lies in front, while for a **convex mirror**, it lies behind the mirror.
 
• **Principal Axis:** An imaginary straight line passing through the **pole** and the **center of curvature**.
 
• **Focal Length (f):** The distance between the **pole** and the **principal focus**. It is exactly half of the **radius of curvature (R)**, represented as **f = R/2**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Spherical Mirrors:**
 
 
• **Concave Mirror:** Also known as a **converging mirror**. It can form both **real and virtual images** depending on the object's position. Used in **shaving mirrors**, **headlights**, and by **dentists**.
 
• **Convex Mirror:** Also known as a **diverging mirror**. It always forms a **virtual, erect, and diminished image**. Used as **rear-view mirrors** in vehicles to provide a wider field of view.
 
 
 
• **Sign Convention:**
 
 
• According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the object is always placed to the **left** of the mirror. Distances measured in the direction of **incident light** are positive, and those opposite are negative.
 
• The focal length of a **concave mirror** is always **negative**, whereas the focal length of a **convex mirror** is always **positive**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Laws of Reflection:**
 
 
• The **angle of incidence** is always equal to the **angle of reflection** (i = r).
 
• The **incident ray**, the **reflected ray**, and the **normal** at the point of incidence all lie in the **same plane**.
 
 
 
• **Image Formation:**
 
 
• To construct a **ray diagram**, at least **two rays** whose paths are known after reflection are required. The intersection of these reflected rays gives the **position of the image** of the point object.
 
• If the rays actually meet, the image is **real and inverted**. If they appear to meet when produced backwards, the image is **virtual and erect**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which condition is essential for a dispersed seed to successfully undergo germination and develop into a seedling?

options.text: Physical separation from the parent flower
Complete decay of the fruit enclosing the seed only.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Presence of appropriate environmental conditions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Seed Germination** is the biological process by which a plant grows from a **seed** after a period of dormancy. For this process to begin, the internal embryo must be activated by external triggers.
 
• The **Presence of appropriate environmental conditions** is the most critical requirement. These conditions primarily include **moisture (water)**, **oxygen**, and a suitable **temperature**. ***Hence, the correct answer is option 2.***
 
• **Physical separation** from the parent flower or plant is part of the **seed dispersal** mechanism, which helps reduce competition for resources. However, separation alone does not guarantee the biological start of growth if the soil or climate is unfavorable. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• While **Sunlight** is essential for **photosynthesis** once the seedling develops leaves, many seeds actually germinate best in **darkness** (under the soil). Only specific "light-sensitive" seeds require exposure to light to break dormancy. Using the word "only" makes the statement scientifically inaccurate. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **decay of the fruit** may help release the seed or provide some initial organic matter, but it is not a standalone essential condition for the physiological process of germination. Many seeds can germinate even if the fruit is manually removed or eaten by animals. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Essential Factors for Germination:**
 
 
• **Water:** Germination begins with **imbibition**, where the seed rapidly absorbs water. This **swells the seed**, ruptures the **seed coat**, and activates **hydrolytic enzymes** that break down stored food.
 
• **Oxygen:** Early germination requires **aerobic respiration**. The seed needs energy to power cell division and growth, which it obtains by oxidizing stored nutrients using oxygen found in **soil pores**.
 
• **Temperature:** Every seed species has an **optimum temperature** range for germination, typically between **25°C and 30°C** for many tropical plants. Extreme cold or heat can inhibit **enzymatic activity**.
 
 
 
• **Seed Structure:**
 
 
• The **Radicle** is the first part of the embryo to emerge, developing into the **primary root** to anchor the plant and absorb water.
 
• The **Plumule** is the embryonic shoot that eventually grows above the ground to form the **stem and leaves**.
 
• **Cotyledons** or the **Endosperm** serve as the primary **food storage** units that nourish the growing seedling until it can perform photosynthesis.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Seed Dormancy:** This is a state where seeds do not germinate even when environmental conditions are favorable. It is a survival strategy to ensure seeds germinate only during the **correct season**.
 
• **Scarification:** This involves breaking or softening the **seed coat** (mechanically or via **acid** in animal guts) to allow water and oxygen to enter.
 
• **Stratification:** Some seeds require a period of **cold treatment** (simulating winter) before they are physiologically ready to germinate in the **spring**.
 
• **Epigeal vs. Hypogeal Germination:** In **Epigeal germination**, the cotyledons are pushed above the ground (e.g., **bean seeds**), whereas in **Hypogeal germination**, the cotyledons remain below the soil (e.g., **pea seeds** or **maize**).

questions.question: Which type of blood vessel has thick, elastic walls to withstand high pressure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Artery**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Arteries** are the blood vessels responsible for carrying blood away from the **heart** to various tissues and organs throughout the body.
 
• Because the heart pumps blood into the arteries with significant force, the blood inside them flows under **high pressure**.
 
• To accommodate this **high pressure**, arteries have **thick, muscular, and elastic walls**. These walls consist of three distinct layers: the **tunica intima**, the **tunica media** (which is notably thick in arteries), and the **tunica externa**.
 
• The **elasticity** of the arterial walls allows them to expand during **systole** (heart contraction) and recoil during **diastole** (heart relaxation), which helps in maintaining a continuous flow of blood even when the heart is not beating.
 
• Unlike veins, most **arteries** do not have **valves** (except for the **semilunar valves** at the base of the **aorta** and the **pulmonary artery**) because the high pressure of the blood prevents it from flowing backward.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Veins**:
 
 
• **Veins** carry blood toward the **heart** from various parts of the body.
 
• Since the blood in veins is no longer under the direct pumping pressure of the heart, it flows at a **lower pressure** compared to arteries.
 
• Consequently, **veins** have **thinner walls** and a **larger lumen** (internal space). They are equipped with **valves** to ensure blood flows in only one direction, preventing **backflow** due to gravity.
 
 
 
• **Capillaries**:
 
 
• **Capillaries** are the smallest and thinnest blood vessels, connecting **arterioles** (small arteries) and **venules** (small veins).
 
• Their walls are extremely thin, usually only **one cell thick** (endothelium), which allows for the **diffusion and exchange** of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nutrients, and waste products between the blood and the surrounding **interstitial fluid**.
 
 
 
• **Venules**:
 
 
• **Venules** are very small blood vessels in the microcirculation that allow blood to return from **capillary beds** to drain into the larger **veins**.
 
 
 
• **Pulmonary Exceptions**:
 
 
• While most arteries carry **oxygenated blood**, the **Pulmonary Artery** is the exception, carrying **deoxygenated blood** from the right ventricle to the **lungs**.
 
• Similarly, the **Pulmonary Vein** carries **oxygenated blood** from the lungs back to the **left atrium** of the heart.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Aorta** is the largest **artery** in the human body, originating from the **left ventricle** and distributing blood to the entire **systemic circulation**.
 
• The **elasticity** of arteries decreases with **age** or due to certain health conditions like **atherosclerosis**, which can lead to increased **blood pressure** (hypertension).
 
• In a healthy adult, the typical **systolic blood pressure** measured in the arteries is about **120 mmHg**, while the **diastolic pressure** is about **80 mmHg**.
 
• The smooth muscle in the **tunica media** of arteries allows them to perform **vasoconstriction** and **vasodilation**, which are essential for regulating **blood flow** and **body temperature**.
</ul

questions.question: Find the median for the data 9, 6, 8, 11, 16, and 22.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Arrange data: 6, 8, 9, 11, 16, 22

Total terms (n) = 6 (Even number)

Median = Average of the two middle terms

Middle terms are 9 and 11

Median = (9 + 11) ÷ 2 = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Data set = 9, 6, 8, 11, 16, 22

**Formula Used:**

If n is even, Median = [ (n/2)th term + (n/2 + 1)th term ] ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/06c79b2175137aff62ffc687a1f9c355fe0ff97d3daa558ea07f37b9388f4e1f.png] 

⇒ Step 1: Arrange data in ascending order: 6, 8, 9, 11, 16, 22

⇒ Step 2: Count the number of observations (n) = 6

⇒ Step 3: Identify the positions of the middle terms

⇒ Position 1 = n/2 = 6/2 = 3rd term

⇒ Position 2 = (n/2) + 1 = 3 + 1 = 4th term

⇒ Step 4: Value of 3rd term = 9 and 4th term = 11

⇒ Median = (9 + 11) ÷ 2

⇒ Median = 20 ÷ 2 = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

Median for Odd Number of Terms

If the total number of terms (n) is odd, the median is the middle-most term located at the ((n + 1)/2)th position after sorting.

Arithmetic Mean

Mean is the sum of all values divided by the number of values. Formula: Σx ÷ n.

Mode of Data

Mode is the value that appears most frequently in the data set. A set can be unimodal, bimodal, or multimodal.

questions.question: In a race, an athlete covers a distance of 450 m in 150 sec in the first lap. He covers the second lap of the same distance in 75 sec. What is the average speed (in m/sec) of the athlete?

When distances are equal, Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) / (S₁ + S₂).

Average Speed = (2 × 3 × 6) / (3 + 6) = 36 / 9 = 4 m/s.

⇒ Total Distance = D₁ + D₂ = 450 + 450 = 900 m

questions.question: If the total surface area of a cylinder is 3080 m² and its radius is 14 m, then what is the curved surface area of the cylinder? (Take pi= (22)/(7))

Total Surface Area (TSA) = Curved Surface Area (CSA) + 2 × Base Area

Base Area = πr² = (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 616 m²

2 × Base Area = 2 × 616 = 1232 m²

CSA = TSA − 2 × Base Area = 3080 − 1232 = 1848 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 1848 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 3080 m²

Radius (r) = 14 m

⇒ h + 14 = 3080 ÷ 88

⇒ h + 14 = 35

⇒ h = 35 − 14 = 21 m

⇒ CSA = 2 × (22/7) × 14 × 21

⇒ CSA = 2 × 22 × 2 × 21

⇒ CSA = 88 × 21

⇒ CSA = 1848 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 1848 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Hollow Cylinder

For a hollow cylinder with outer radius R and inner radius r, TSA = 2πh(R + r) + 2π(R² − r²).

Base Perimeter

The perimeter or circumference of the base of a cylinder is 2πr, which when multiplied by height gives the CSA.</p

questions.question: The ratio of the sum of exterior angles to the sum of interior angles of a regular polygon of n sides is 2 : 43. What is the measure of an interior angle of the regular polygon?

questions.question: If the length of a rectangle is 5 cm more than the breadth and if the perimeter of the rectangle is 40 cm, then the length and breadth of the rectangle will be:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of Length (L) and Breadth (B) = Perimeter ÷ 2 = 40 ÷ 2 = 20 cm.

Difference between Length and Breadth (L − B) = 5 cm.

Length (L) = (Sum + Difference) ÷ 2 = (20 + 5) ÷ 2 = 12.5 cm.

Breadth (B) = (Sum − Difference) ÷ 2 = (20 − 5) ÷ 2 = 7.5 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5 cm, 7.5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Perimeter (P) = 40 cm

Length (L) = Breadth (B) + 5 cm

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of a rectangle = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/957a9e59d69ace4f9fea4f024a0c3ad88512088df6fadf02f5231a2a6f8b3db3.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × (L + B) = 40

⇒ L + B = 20

⇒ (B + 5) + B = 20

⇒ 2B + 5 = 20

⇒ 2B = 20 − 5

⇒ 2B = 15

⇒ B = 7.5 cm

⇒ L = B + 5 = 7.5 + 5 = 12.5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5 cm, 7.5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Rectangle

The total space occupied by the rectangle is given by Area = Length × Breadth.

Diagonal of Rectangle

The distance between opposite corners is d = √(L² + B²).

Square Property

A rectangle becomes a square when Length = Breadth, and its perimeter is 4 × Side.</p

questions.question: A retailer offers the following discount schemes for buyers on an article. Which scheme will fetch the maximum selling price?

Maximum Selling Price is obtained when the total effective discount is minimum.

Check the sum of discounts for each scheme: (1) 38%, (2) 58%, (3) 61%, (4) 20%.

Since Scheme 4 has the lowest sum and lowest individual values, its effective discount will be the minimum.

Minimum Discount ⇒ Maximum Selling Price.

For a fixed sum of two discounts (a+b = constant), the effective discount is maximum when the difference between a and b is maximum, and minimum when the difference is minimum.</p

Recognize x = 3 + 2√2 as a perfect square: (√2 + 1)².

Value = 2.

questions.question: The price of each article of types P, Q, and R is ₹280, ₹185, and ₹105, respectively. Yogesh buys articles of each type in the ratio 4 : 2 : 5 and spends a total of ₹8,060. How many articles of type Q did he purchase?

Common multiplier = Total budget ÷ Unit cost = 8060 ÷ 2015 = 4

questions.question: By decreasing the radius of a sphere by 25% whose surface area is 616 cm² , a new sphere is formed. Find the volume of the newly formed sphere. (Take pi = (22)/(7) )
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Surface Area (SA) = 4πr² = 616 ⇒ r² = 49 ⇒ r = 7 cm.

Radius decreases by 25% ⇒ Ratio of radii = 1 : 0.75 = 4 : 3.

Ratio of volumes = (4)³ : (3)³ = 64 : 27.

Original Volume = (4/3) × (22/7) × 7³ = 4312/3 cm³.

New Volume = (4312/3) × (27/64) = 135.375 × 4.48 ≈ 606.375 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 606.375 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Surface area of the original sphere = 616 cm²

Reduction in radius = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Surface area of sphere = 4πr²

Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0e5b328b6188edabbe6569d9d604fdcfbfcc71b4495edf788588fd09e08a8d8b.png] 

Step 1: Finding the radius of the original sphere (r).

⇒ 4 × (22/7) × r² = 616

⇒ r² = (616 × 7) / (4 × 22)

⇒ r² = (616 × 7) / 88

⇒ r² = 7 × 7 = 49

⇒ r = 7 cm

Step 2: Finding the radius of the new sphere (rₙₑw).

⇒ rₙₑw = r − 25% of r

⇒ rₙₑw = 7 − (25/100 × 7)

⇒ rₙₑw = 7 − 1.75 = 5.25 cm

Step 3: Finding the volume of the new sphere.

⇒ Volume = (4/3) × π × (rₙₑw)³

⇒ Volume = (4/3) × (22/7) × (5.25) × (5.25) × (5.25)

⇒ Volume = (4/3) × (22/7) × (21/4) × (21/4) × (21/4)

⇒ Volume = (22 × 21 × 21) / (4 × 4)

⇒ Volume = (11 × 441) / 8 = 4851 / 8

⇒ Volume = 606.375 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 606.375 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Sphere

For a sphere of radius r, the Surface Area is 4πr² and the Volume is (4/3)πr³.

Ratio Relationship

If the radius of a sphere is changed by a factor of k, the surface area changes by k² and the volume changes by k³.

Hemisphere Calculations

For a hemisphere, the Curved Surface Area is 2πr² and the Total Surface Area is 3πr².</p

questions.question: Simplify (5pq + 16q)² - (5pq - 16q)² .
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Apply the algebraic identity: (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab.

In this expression, a = 5pq and b = 16q.

Required value = 4 × 5pq × 16q = 320pq².

**∴ The correct answer is 320pq².**

Formula used: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²

⇒ [25p²q² + 160pq² + 256q²] − [25p²q² − 160pq² + 256q²]

⇒ 25p²q² + 160pq² + 256q² − 25p²q² + 160pq² − 256q²

⇒ 160pq² + 160pq²

⇒ 320pq²

**∴ The correct answer is 320pq².**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity for Difference of Squares

x² − y² = (x + y)(x − y). This can also be used to solve the problem by letting x = (5pq + 16q) and y = (5pq − 16q).

Algebraic Identity for Sum of Squares

(a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²). This identity is used when the middle sign is positive.

Simplification Rule

While simplifying algebraic expressions, always check for common factors or standard identities to reduce calculation time.</p

questions.question: Which pioneering molecular biologist, who co-discovered the double helix structure of DNA along with Francis H. C. Crick and was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1962, passed away at the age of 97 in East Northport, New York?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**James D. Watson**__.

__
 
• **James Dewey Watson** is an American **molecular biologist**, geneticist, and zoologist, best known for being one of the co-discoverers of the **structure of DNA** in **1953**.
 
• He, along with **Francis Crick** and **Maurice Wilkins**, was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine** in **1962** for their discoveries concerning the molecular structure of nucleic acids and its significance for information transfer in living material.
 
• Watson's career was marked by his tenure at the **University of Cambridge's Cavendish Laboratory**, where he collaborated with Crick to model the **double helix** structure of **Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA)**.
 
• Beyond his research, he served as the **director** of the **Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory (CSHL)** in **New York** for many years, significantly expanding its research in cancer and neurobiology.
 
• He played a pivotal role in the **Human Genome Project**, serving as the first director of the **National Center for Human Genome Research** at the **National Institutes of Health (NIH)** starting in **1988**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Francis H. C. Crick:**
 
 
• A British **molecular biologist** and physicist who worked closely with Watson. He is also famous for proposing the **Central Dogma** of molecular biology, which describes the flow of genetic information from **DNA to RNA to protein**.
 
 
 
• **Rosalind Franklin:**
 
 
• A British **chemist** and X-ray crystallographer whose data was critical to the discovery. Her **Photo 51**, an X-ray diffraction image of DNA, provided the essential clues for the **helical structure**. She passed away in **1958** at the **age of 37** and was not eligible for the Nobel Prize posthumously.
 
 
 
• **Maurice Wilkins:**
 
 
• A New Zealand-born British **biophysicist** who shared the **1962 Nobel Prize**. He headed the team at **King's College London** where the X-ray diffraction studies of DNA were primarily conducted.
 
 
 
• **The Double Helix Discovery:**
 
 
• The discovery published in the journal **Nature** in **April 1953** explained how genetic information is stored and replicated. It revealed that **DNA** consists of two strands winding around each other, held together by **nitrogenous bases** (Adenine, Thymine, Guanine, and Cytosine).

• **Legacy:** Despite later controversies regarding his public statements, his scientific contributions remain a cornerstone of **modern biology** and **biotechnology**.
