The correct answer is __**Hydropower generation and irrigation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kulsi Multipurpose Project** is a major water resource initiative proposed on the **Kulsi River**, which is a significant south-bank tributary of the **Brahmaputra River**.
 
• The primary objective of the project is the **generation of hydropower** and the provision of **irrigation** facilities to enhance agricultural productivity in the region. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• The project is not primarily aimed at **Military infrastructure**, as its design focuses on socio-economic development and civil utility. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• While **Industrial development** might be an indirect beneficiary of the electricity generated, it is not listed as the project's primary functional purpose. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Although large water bodies often attract visitors, **Tourism promotion** is a secondary byproduct and not the core mandate like irrigation and power. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The project is planned to have an installed capacity of approximately **55 MW** of **hydropower**, contributing significantly to the energy grid of **Assam** and **Meghalaya**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographic Location:** The **Kulsi River** originates in the **Khasi Hills** of **Meghalaya** and flows through the **Kamrup district** of **Assam** before joining the **Brahmaputra**. The dam site is typically proposed near **Ukiam**, located at the border of the two states.
 
• **Irrigation Scope:** The project aims to provide irrigation to over **24,000 hectares** to **40,000 hectares** of land, supporting farmers during both the **Kharif** and **Rabi** seasons.
 
• **Flood Moderation:** Apart from power and water for crops, the project serves the critical function of **flood control**. It helps in regulating the discharge of water during the heavy **Monsoon** months, reducing the risk of downstream flooding in **Assam**.
 
• **National Project Status:** Due to its scale and regional importance, the **Kulsi Project** has been considered for **National Project** status, which allows for a **90:10** funding pattern between the **Central Government** and the state.
 
• **Environmental Significance:** The river is one of the few remaining habitats for the endangered **Gangetic River Dolphin** (Platanista gangetica), making the ecological impact assessment of this project a vital administrative and environmental concern.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Implementing Agencies:** The project planning and Detailed Project Reports (DPR) are often handled by the **Brahmaputra Board** under the **Ministry of Jal Shakti**, Government of India.
 
• **Inter-state Coordination:** Since the river flows through both **Assam** and **Meghalaya**, the project requires a high degree of cooperation regarding land acquisition and benefit-sharing between the two state governments.
 
• **Socio-Economic Impact:** By providing stable **electricity** and **water**, the project is expected to boost the local economy, improve **livelihoods**, and provide a buffer against the erratic nature of rainfall in the **North-Eastern** region of **India**.
</ul

questions.question: Inaugurated in September 2025, the Monopropellant Thruster Test Facility (MPTTF) primarily supports testing activities related to which broad technological domain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Space propulsion systems**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Monopropellant Thruster Test Facility (MPTTF)** was officially inaugurated in **September 2025** to serve as a specialized hub for evaluating advanced **Space propulsion systems**.
 
• The facility is primarily designed to conduct rigorous testing of **low-thrust monopropellant engines**, which are essential for the **Reaction Control Systems (RCS)** and **Attitude and Orbit Control Systems (AOCS)** of various spacecraft.
 
• Equipped with high-performance **vacuum chambers**, the MPTTF can simulate the extreme conditions of **outer space**, allowing engineers to measure critical parameters such as **Specific Impulse (Isp)**, **Thrust**, and **Thermal Management**.
 
• The establishment of this facility marks a significant milestone in achieving **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-reliant India) in the space sector, reducing dependency on international testing labs for **satellite propulsion** validation.
 
• Testing at MPTTF focuses on the reliability of **catalyst beds** and **propellant feed systems**, ensuring that thrusters can perform thousands of **pulses** over a mission lifespan of **10 to 15 years**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Monopropellant Technology:**
 
 
• A **monopropellant** is a chemical propellant that consists of a single substance or a mixture of chemicals that decomposes or reacts when exposed to a **catalyst**.
 
• Unlike bipropellant systems, it does not require a separate **oxidizer**, making the propulsion system simpler, lighter, and more **reliable**.
 
• **Anhydrous Hydrazine** is the most commonly used monopropellant in the industry due to its stable storage and predictable performance characteristics.
 
 
 
• **Applications in Satellites:**
 
 
• These systems are vital for **Station Keeping** (maintaining the satellite's assigned position in orbit) and **Momentum Dumping**.
 
• They are extensively used in **Geostationary Satellites (GEO)** and **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)** constellations for precise **manoeuvring**.
 
 
 
• **Emerging Green Propellants:**
 
 
• Modern facilities like MPTTF are increasingly being adapted to test **Green Propellants** such as **Hydroxylammonium Nitrate (HAN)** and **Ammonium Dinitramide (ADN)**.
 
• These alternatives are **less toxic** and more environmentally friendly compared to traditional **Hydrazine**, reducing the **hazard costs** associated with fueling operations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Precision Testing:** The facility can measure very small thrust values, often in the range of **1 Newton to 22 Newtons**, which are standard for **Micro-satellites** and **Nano-satellites**.
 
• **Operational Readiness:** By providing a localized testing environment, the facility accelerates the **Time-to-Market** for private space startups and **Government space agencies**.
 
• **Data Acquisition:** It utilizes high-speed **data acquisition systems** to monitor the **catalytic decomposition** process, which occurs at temperatures exceeding **800 degrees Celsius**.
 
• **Strategic Impact:** The MPTTF supports the growth of the **Commercial Space** sector, particularly in the development of **satellite buses** for global customers under the **NewSpace India** initiatives.
</ul

questions.question: Which category of climate finance did India argue should be scaled up *independently* during the post-COP-30 negotiations held in November 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Adaptation finance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the post-**COP-30** negotiations held in **November 2025**, **India** strongly advocated for the **independent scaling up** of **Adaptation finance**. **India** argued that funding for building resilience must be distinct and not overshadowed by **mitigation** efforts.
 
• The demand was made in the context of the **New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG)**, which is the new financial target intended to succeed the **$100 billion** annual pledge made by developed nations. **India** emphasized that **adaptation** is a matter of survival for **developing countries** and requires predictable, grant-based public funding.
 
• **India** pointed out that **adaptation** projects often lack the commercial appeal of **mitigation** (such as **renewable energy**), making it difficult to attract private capital. Therefore, a separate and **scaled-up** allocation is necessary to address the specific needs of the **Global South**.
 
• The negotiations highlighted the **doubling of adaptation finance** pledge made at **COP-26** in **Glasgow**, with **India** insisting that this target must be met and significantly expanded post-**2025**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Adaptation finance.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Adaptation vs. Mitigation:** 
 
 
• **Mitigation** refers to efforts to reduce or prevent the emission of **greenhouse gases**, such as transitioning to **solar** or **wind energy**.
 
• **Adaptation** involves taking action to prepare for and adjust to both the current effects of **climate change** and the predicted impacts in the future, such as building **flood defenses** or developing **drought-resistant crops**.
 
 
 
• **COP-30 (Conference of the Parties):** 
 
 
• The **30th United Nations Climate Change Conference** took place in **Belém, Brazil**, in **November 2025**. It was a landmark summit focusing on the **Amazon rainforest** and the **Global Goal on Adaptation (GGA)**.
 
• The summit aimed to finalize the **NCQG**, ensuring that trillions of dollars are mobilized for **climate action** in **vulnerable nations**.
 
 
 
• **Global Goal on Adaptation (GGA):** 
 
 
• Established under the **Paris Agreement** (**Article 7**), the **GGA** aims to enhance adaptive capacity, strengthen resilience, and reduce vulnerability to **climate change**.
 
• During **2024-2025**, the focus shifted toward establishing clear indicators to measure progress in **adaptation** globally.
 
 
 
• **India's Domestic Framework:** 
 
 
• **India** implements its **adaptation** strategies through the **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)**, which includes **eight national missions** covering water, agriculture, and Himalayan ecosystems.
 
• The **National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change (NAFCC)** was established in **2015-16** to assist states and union territories that are particularly vulnerable to the adverse effects of **climate change**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Loss and Damage Finance:** Unlike **adaptation** (which is proactive), **Loss and Damage** finance refers to compensation for the unavoidable and irreversible impacts of **climate change** that have already occurred. The **Loss and Damage Fund** was operationalized at **COP-28**.
 
• **Climate Finance Gap:** The **UNEP Adaptation Gap Report** frequently highlights that the costs of **adaptation** in **developing countries** are **5 to 10 times** greater than current public **adaptation finance** flows.
 
• **CBDR-RC:** **India’s** stance is rooted in the principle of **Common But Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC)**, which holds **developed countries** historically responsible for **emissions** and thus obligated to provide **financial resources**.
 
• **Article 9 of the Paris Agreement:** This article stipulates that **developed country Parties** shall provide **financial resources** to assist **developing country Parties** with respect to both **mitigation** and **adaptation**.

questions.question: Which Vietnamese-American author released 'The Emperor of Gladness' in May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ocean Vuong**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ocean Vuong**, a celebrated **Vietnamese-American** author, is the creator of the novel titled **'The Emperor of Gladness'**, which saw its release in **May 2025**.
 
• The book is a highly anticipated work of fiction following his monumental success in both the realms of **poetry** and **prose**.
 
• The narrative of **'The Emperor of Gladness'** focuses on the relationship between a young man and an elderly person struggling with **memory loss**, exploring themes of care, loneliness, and human connection.
 
• **Ocean Vuong** has established himself as a prominent voice in contemporary **American literature**, known for his lyrical and emotionally resonant writing style that often bridges his identity as a **poet** with his narrative storytelling. ***Hence, the statement regarding his authorship of this book is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Literary Career and Major Works:**
 
 
• **Ocean Vuong** gained international acclaim with his debut novel, **'On Earth We're Briefly Gorgeous'**, published in **2019**. The novel is framed as a letter from a son to his illiterate mother and explores the legacy of the **Vietnam War**.
 
• In the field of poetry, his collection **'Night Sky with Exit Wounds'** (**2016**) won the **T.S. Eliot Prize** and the **Whiting Award**.
 
• His subsequent poetry collection, **'Time is a Mother'**, was released in **2022**, further cementing his reputation for exploring grief and family history.
 
 
 
• **Biography and Background:**
 
 
• Born in **1988** in **Saigon, Vietnam** (now **Ho Chi Minh City**), he immigrated to the **United States** at the **age of two** after spending time in a **refugee camp** in **the Philippines**.
 
• He grew up in **Hartford, Connecticut**, and his experiences as a **first-generation immigrant** and a **queer man** of color are central themes in his literary output.
 
• In **2019**, he was awarded the prestigious **MacArthur Fellowship**, commonly known as the **"Genius Grant,"** for his contributions to literature.
 
 
 
• **Context of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Colum McCann**: An **Irish** writer known for novels like **'Let the Great World Spin'** and **'Apeirogon'**.
 
• **Charlotte McConaghy**: An **Australian** author recognized for her works **'Migrations'** and **'Once There Were Wolves'**, which often focus on environmental and nature-driven themes.
 
• **Sharon Lee**: Often associated with **science fiction** and the **Liaden universe** series, representing a different genre entirely from Vuong's literary fiction.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Theme of the Book:** The novel **'The Emperor of Gladness'** signifies a shift or continuation in Vuong's exploration of **vulnerability** and **intergenerational bonds**.
 
• **Release Timeline:** The **May 2025** release was one of the most significant literary events of the year, highlighting the enduring popularity of **Asian-American** narratives in the global market.
 
• **Style:** Vuong is often cited for his **autofictional** elements, though his **2025** release demonstrates a deepening of his fictional world-building and character studies.
